data.raw_text:
On January 27, 2026, Private Kioni Peoples was involved in a motorcycle accident in Bakersfield, California and was airlifted to a trauma center in Las Vegas.

By the time Kioni’s father, Eddie Peoples, was able to arrive at the hospital after a 28-hour flight from the Philippines, Kioni had worsened and doctors were assessing him for brain death.

Doctors performed several neurological checks: testing reflex responses, checking eye movements, and evaluating reactions to stimuli. A breathing test followed, in which the ventilator was removed to see if Kioni would breathe independently.

After several minutes, the doctor reportedly described the results as “inconclusive.”

The family expected additional testing to follow as the medical team had previously mentioned a nuclear brain blood flow test.

But according to Eddie, that test never happened. Instead, shortly after the initial examination, the doctor returned and informed the family that Kioni met the criteria for brain death.

The family was then escorted into a room to meet with someone they were told was a hospital representative, but who turned out to be an employee of the local organ procurement organization. She told them that Kioni had chosen to be an organ donor, and that his organs would be harvested.

The family was shocked. According to Eddie, neither Kioni’s military ID nor his driver’s license indicated an organ donor status. Organ donation had also been a topic the family had discussed before, and they believed Kioni shared their reservations.

But in the absence of a documented healthcare power of attorney and a specific refusal to donate, the family was helpless, and Kioni became an organ donor. 

Every family should not only discuss their end-of-life wishes, they should document them. A life-affirming healthcare power of attorney document is linked below.
